response.sql: WITH team_stats AS (SELECT team_id, SUM(w) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT year) AS avg_wins, AVG((g - l) * 1.0 / NULLIF(l, 0)) AS avg_gl_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), mean_wins AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_avg_wins FROM team_stats) SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_wins, t.avg_gl_ratio, t.avg_wins - m.mean_avg_wins AS gap FROM team_stats t CROSS JOIN mean_wins m WHERE t.avg_wins > m.mean_avg_wins ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Each team's seasons are counted as COUNT(DISTINCT year) over all of its manager_half rows, and total wins is SUM(w), so a season split into two halves or multiple managers counts once for the season and its wins are summed across rows.
Rows with l = 0 are treated as missing in the (games − losses) ÷ losses average (NULLIF(l, 0)), since division by zero is undefined; NULL g or l values are skipped by AVG.
The mean of all teams' average wins is an unweighted AVG over the per-team averages, computed over teams with a non-null average, and the cutoff is strictly greater than that mean.
team_id is used as-is, with no merging of renamed franchises and no separation by league_id.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only seasons in which the team has a non-null win total as the denominator for average wins, so seasons with missing w values do not lower the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH team_stats AS (SELECT team_id, SUM(w) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN w IS NOT NULL THEN year END) AS avg_wins, AVG((g - l) * 1.0 / NULLIF(l, 0)) AS avg_gl_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), mean_wins AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_avg_wins FROM team_stats) SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_wins, t.avg_gl_ratio, t.avg_wins - m.mean_avg_wins AS gap FROM team_stats t CROSS JOIN mean_wins m WHERE t.avg_wins > m.mean_avg_wins ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
